environment: Great Barrier Reef gears up for its spring coral spawning spectacular
Queensland rooftop solar uptake keeps climbing as spring sunshine returns
science: Aussie researchers edge closer to a faster, cheaper test for early disease detection
sports: Bathurst buzz builds as the Great Race returns to Mount Panorama this long weekend
stories.overview: Communities across the south east pitch in for a massive spring clean up of local waterways

segments.title: The Open
segments.script: G'day legends, welcome back to ParkSyde Bright Side, I'm Alex Mercer and it is a ripper of a Saturday out there. Spring's well and truly kicked in and honestly the vibe today is just good news wall to wall. It really is, I'm Jamie and I've been grinning at my notes all morning. We've got reef magic, solar wins, a health breakthrough, motorsport madness and a community clean up that'll warm your heart. Plus Sam's got the weather sorted for everyone heading out and about this weekend. So grab a cuppa, settle in, let's get into it.

segments.title: Green Desk
segments.script: Right, environment first, and it's reef season baby. Marine scientists reckon the Great Barrier Reef is just about ready for its annual coral spawning, that wild once a year event where the reef basically throws a confetti party underwater. Yeah it's one of those things that still blows my mind, millions of coral polyps releasing eggs and sperm into the water on the same night, all triggered by the moon and the water temp. Nature's timing is better than my alarm clock. Citizen science crews up and down the coast are gearing up to help monitor it too, which is such a lovely reminder that everyday Queenslanders get to play a part in looking after the reef. And speaking of sunny things, solar's having a moment as well.

segments.title: Science & Tomorrow
segments.script: Alright science corner, and this one's actually pretty exciting. Aussie researchers are chipping away at a new kind of test that could flag certain diseases way earlier than what's currently on offer, and cheaper too. Earlier detection basically means better outcomes across the board, that's the whole game in medicine isn't it. Catch it quick, treat it quick, everyone's happier including your wallet and your GP. Exactly, and it's the kind of quiet, patient lab work that doesn't always make headlines but ends up changing lives down the track. We'll keep you posted as that research rolls on.

segments.title: Weather
segments.script: Cheers Alex, g'day everyone, Sam here with your south east Queensland weather. Today's shaping up warm and mostly sunny across Brisbane, the Gold Coast and the Sunshine Coast, top temps sitting in the mid to high twenties with just a bit of a breeze to keep things comfortable. We might see a few fluffy clouds building inland through the afternoon, with a small chance of an isolated shower or storm out west of the ranges, but coastal areas should stay dry for anyone heading to the beach or the footy. Overnight it'll cool down nicely into the high teens, perfect sleeping weather, and we're tracking a similar pattern through the rest of the weekend with temps gradually creeping up as we head into next week. Back to you Alex and Jamie.

segments.title: The Scoreboard
segments.script: Sports time, and if you can hear a faint rumble today that's not thunder, that's Mount Panorama warming up for the Bathurst 1000. The Great Race is back this long weekend and the whole town of Bathurst basically turns into one giant motorsport festival. Love this time of year, there's nothing quite like The Mountain, a thousand kays, drivers pushing their cars and their nerves to the absolute limit. Even if you're not a petrolhead it's hard not to get swept up in it. And with the footy finals season also wrapping up around the country, it's just a cracking stretch for Aussie sport generally. Plenty to cheer for whether you're trackside or on the couch with snacks.

segments.title: Overview & Outro
segments.script: Now before we go, our feel good story of the day, and it's a proper community one. Volunteers across the south east have been turning out in big numbers for a spring clean up of local creeks and waterways. I love this one, everyday people grabbing gloves and bin bags on a Saturday morning just because they care about their local patch. Little kids, grandparents, whole families out there together. It's such a simple thing but it adds up, cleaner waterways, healthier wildlife, and a real sense of neighbourhood pride. That's the ParkSyde spirit right there. Couldn't have said it better. That's it for today's Bright Side, thanks so much for hanging out with us, I'm Jamie. And I'm Alex, get out there and enjoy that sunshine Queensland, we'll catch you next time on ParkSyde Bright Side.
